caveats: covarying (mzLib's PtmPairEngine.CoVarying, type A): Spearman's rho of two sites' occupancies across runs. With --include-bounds, a run where a site was seen in only one form enters as a bound, never as an invented value: not_detected (a covered-zero) and floor cells tie below every fraction of that site, and a ceiling, or a count_only cell whose covering peptidoforms all carry the modification, ties above every fraction. A count_only cell where both forms were identified has no rank and is left out. Bounds count toward min_quantified_fraction.
A site enters co-varying pairs only if it has a value or a bound in at least min_quantified_fraction of covarying_run_count, the runs (or samples) where any site was identified or covered.

With --include-bounds, a pair is tested only if at least one of its sites has at least min_untied_share (0.5) of the shared runs outside its largest tie of bounds; otherwise test_status is both_sites_mostly_bounds and it has no statistic, p_value or q. mzLib's reason: when both sites are mostly one bound, Spearman's t test calls 2 to 5 times too many pairs at p < 0.001 with no relation at all (mzLib's simulation, PtmPairEngine.MinUntiedShare).

q is Benjamini-Hochberg within fdr_family (the type, then intra or inter protein). An overlapping pair, two sites one peptide covers, is reported but left out of the family (q null): shared peptides correlate it by construction. q is not a target-decoy q-value.
p_value is Spearman's two-sided p, exact for 9 or fewer runs without ties, otherwise asymptotic (t on n - 2 degrees of freedom), as stats correlate reports it.

The observations follow ptmqtl occupancy's rules: MS/MS identifications only, one row per (run, peptidoform, protein), and the same exclusions (Common Variable, Common Fixed, peptide-terminal and C-terminal modifications).
